name: Defensores del Chaco National Park
blurb: Thorn forest, cacti and Cerro Leon, with jaguar and puma on top.

tip.title: Remove the jaguar
tip.text: Jaguars and pumas prey on peccaries, tapirs and brockets. Set Jaguar to -100% and watch the herbivores and what they eat shift.

sources.title: Wikipedia: National Parks in the Paraguayan Chaco
UNESCO tentative list: Defensores del Chaco

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Strong subtropical sun drives plant growth on the open Chaco plain, but it also dries the land through the long dry season.
Rain falls mostly in one wet season followed by a long dry spell, so plant growth and water for animals come in pulses.
Sandy and clay soils of the plain hold the nutrients that trees and grasses draw on, topped up as dead matter breaks down.

nodes.name: Fungi, bacteria and termites
nodes.desc: Break down fallen wood, leaf litter and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.
A large browsing mammal that eats leaves and fruit and spreads seeds through its dung.
Colonies cut leaves to grow fungus underground, moving plant matter into the soil.
A common scavenger that cleans up carcasses across open country and woodland.
The largest cat of the Americas. The park may hold one of the southernmost viable jaguar populations; it hunts peccaries, tapirs and deer.
A widespread cat reported with a viable population in the park; it preys on deer, peccaries and armadillos.
